source: AWS Certified AI Practitioner (AIF-C01) Exam Guide, docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/ai-practitioner-01/, version 1.1 (April 30, 2026). Checked October 6, 2026.

domains.name: Fundamentals of AI and ML
domains.plain: What AI, machine learning, and deep learning are, how models learn, and how we measure them.

domains.name: Fundamentals of GenAI
domains.plain: How language models and other generative models work, what they're good at, where they fail, and what AWS offers.

domains.name: Applications of Foundation Models
domains.plain: Prompting, RAG, agents, choosing a model, fine-tuning, and evaluating what you built.

domains.name: Guidelines for Responsible AI
domains.plain: Fairness, bias, transparency, human oversight, and the legal risks of generative AI.

domains.name: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
domains.plain: Who secures what on AWS, least privilege, logging, and the rules and frameworks that apply.

tasks.title: Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
Identify practical use cases for AI
Explain the basic concepts of generative AI (GenAI)
Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
Describe AWS infrastructure and technologies for building GenAI applications
Describe design considerations for applications that use foundation models (FMs)
Describe the training and fine-tuning process for FMs
Describe methods to evaluate FM performance
Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
Explain methods to secure AI systems
Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems

objectives.text: Define basic AI terms
objectives.examples: AI, ML, deep learning, neural networks, computer vision, natural language processing (NLP), model, algorithm, training and inferencing, bias, fairness, fit, large language model (LLM), generative AI (GenAI), agentic AI

objectives.text: Describe the similarities and differences between AI, ML, GenAI, deep learning, and agentic AI
Describe various types of inferencing
objectives.examples: batch, real-time, asynchronous, serverless

objectives.text: Describe the different types of data in AI models
objectives.examples: labeled and unlabeled, tabular, time-series, image, text, structured and unstructured

objectives.text: Describe different types of AI/ML learning
objectives.examples: supervised learning, unsupervised learning, reinforcement learning methods

objectives.text: Recognize applications where AI/ML can provide value
objectives.examples: assist human decision making, solution scalability, automation

objectives.text: Determine when AI/ML solutions are not appropriate
objectives.examples: cost-benefit analyses, situations when a specific outcome is needed instead of a prediction

objectives.text: Select the appropriate AI/ML techniques for specific use cases
objectives.examples: regression, classification, clustering

objectives.text: Identify examples of real-world AI applications
objectives.examples: computer vision, NLP, speech recognition, recommendation systems, fraud detection, forecasting, knowledge bases, agentic AI

objectives.text: Explain the capabilities of AWS managed AI/ML services
objectives.examples: Amazon SageMaker AI, Amazon Transcribe, Amazon Translate, Amazon Comprehend, Amazon Lex, Amazon Polly

objectives.text: Identify when traditional ML models or foundation models (FMs) are appropriate for a specific use case
objectives.examples: based on regulatory concerns, explainability requirements, operational constraints

objectives.text: Describe and differentiate components of an AI/ML pipeline
Describe sources of FM models
objectives.examples: open source pre-trained models, training custom models

objectives.text: Describe methods to use a model in production
objectives.examples: managed API service, self-hosted API

objectives.text: Identify relevant AWS services and features for each stage of an AI/ML pipeline
objectives.examples: Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Quick, Kiro, SageMaker AI

objectives.text: Describe fundamental concepts of ML operations (MLOps)
objectives.examples: experimentation, repeatable processes, scalable systems, managing technical debt, achieving production readiness, model monitoring, model re-training

objectives.text: Describe model performance metrics and business metrics to evaluate ML models
objectives.examples: accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score; cost per user, development costs, customer feedback, return on investment (ROI)

objectives.text: Define foundational GenAI concepts
objectives.examples: tokens, chunking, embeddings, vectors, prompt engineering, transformer-based LLMs, foundation models (FMs), multi-modal models, diffusion models

objectives.text: Identify potential use cases for GenAI models
objectives.examples: image, video, and audio generation; summarization; AI assistants; translation; code generation; customer service agents; search; recommendation engines

objectives.text: Describe the FM lifecycle
objectives.examples: data selection, model selection, pre-training, fine-tuning, evaluation, deployment, feedback

objectives.text: Describe the token-based pricing model and its effect on cost and performance for inference
Describe the role of context engineering in FM applications
Define foundational agentic AI concepts
objectives.examples: multi-agent system patterns, Model Context Protocol (MCP) and its role in connecting agents to external systems, multi-agent communication patterns, memory management, tool usage, workflow orchestration

objectives.text: Describe the advantages of GenAI
objectives.examples: adaptability, responsiveness, conversational capabilities, ability to generate content

objectives.text: Identify disadvantages of GenAI solutions
objectives.examples: hallucinations, interpretability, inaccuracy, nondeterminism

objectives.text: Identify factors to consider when selecting GenAI models
objectives.examples: model types, performance requirements, capabilities, constraints, compliance, cost, latency, model complexity

objectives.text: Determine business value and metrics for GenAI applications
objectives.examples: cross-domain performance, ROI, efficiency, conversion rate, average revenue per user, accuracy, customer lifetime value

objectives.text: Identify AWS services and features to develop GenAI applications
objectives.examples: Amazon Bedrock, Amazon SageMaker AI, SageMaker JumpStart, Amazon Quick, Kiro, Strands Agents, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

objectives.text: Describe the advantages of using AWS GenAI services to build applications
objectives.examples: accessibility, lower barrier to entry, efficiency, cost-effectiveness, speed to market, ability to meet business objectives

objectives.text: Describe the benefits of AWS infrastructure for GenAI applications
objectives.examples: security, compliance, responsibility, safety

objectives.text: Describe cost tradeoffs of AWS GenAI services
objectives.examples: responsiveness, availability, redundancy, performance, regional coverage, token-based pricing, provisioned throughput, custom models

objectives.text: Identify selection criteria to choose FMs
objectives.examples: cost, modality, latency, multi-lingual, model size, model complexity, customization, input/output length, prompt caching

objectives.text: Describe the effect of inference parameters on model responses
objectives.examples: temperature, input/output length

objectives.text: Define Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) and describe its business applications
objectives.examples: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases

objectives.text: Identify AWS services that help store embeddings within vector databases
objectives.examples: Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon Aurora, Amazon Neptune, Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL

objectives.text: Explain the cost tradeoffs of various approaches to FM customization
objectives.examples: pre-training, fine-tuning, in-context learning, RAG, model distillation

objectives.text: Define the role of AI agents and describe AI agents' business applications
Define the concepts and constructs of prompt engineering
objectives.examples: context, instruction, negative prompts

objectives.text: Define techniques for prompt engineering
objectives.examples: chain-of-thought, zero-shot, single-shot, few-shot, prompt templates

objectives.text: Identify and describe the benefits and best practices for prompt engineering
objectives.examples: response quality improvement, experimentation, guardrails, discovery, specificity and concision, using multiple comments

objectives.text: Define potential risks and limitations of prompt engineering
objectives.examples: exposure, poisoning, hijacking, jailbreaking

objectives.text: Describe prompt versioning and management strategies that use Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management
Describe the key elements of training an FM
objectives.examples: pre-training, fine-tuning, continuous pre-training, distillation

objectives.text: Define methods for fine-tuning an FM
objectives.examples: instruction tuning, adapting models for specific domains, transfer learning, continuous pre-training

objectives.text: Describe how to prepare data to fine-tune an FM
objectives.examples: data curation, governance, size, labeling, representativeness, reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF)

objectives.text: Determine approaches to evaluate FM performance
objectives.examples: human-in-the-loop evaluation, benchmark datasets, Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation

objectives.text: Identify relevant metrics to assess FM performance
objectives.examples: ROUGE, BLEU, BERTScore, LLM-as-a-judge

objectives.text: Determine whether an FM effectively meets business objectives
objectives.examples: productivity, user engagement, task engineering

objectives.text: Identify approaches to evaluate the performance of applications built with FMs
objectives.examples: RAG, agents, workflows

objectives.text: Identify business objective alignment metrics for AI applications
objectives.examples: task completion rate, user satisfaction, cost per interaction

objectives.text: Identify features of responsible AI
objectives.examples: bias, fairness, inclusivity, robustness, safety, veracity

objectives.text: Explain how to use tools to identify features of responsible AI
objectives.examples: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails

objectives.text: Define responsible practices to select a model
objectives.examples: environmental considerations, sustainability

objectives.text: Identify legal risks of working with generative AI (GenAI)
objectives.examples: intellectual property infringement claims, biased model outputs, loss of customer trust, end user risk, hallucinations

objectives.text: Identify characteristics of datasets
objectives.examples: inclusivity, diversity, curated data sources, balanced datasets

objectives.text: Describe effects of bias and variance
objectives.examples: effects on demographic groups, inaccuracy, overfitting, underfitting

objectives.text: Describe tools to detect and monitor bias, trustworthiness, and truthfulness
objectives.examples: analyzing label quality, human audits, subgroup analysis

objectives.text: Describe the differences between models that are transparent and explainable and models that are not
Describe tools to identify transparent and explainable models
objectives.examples: Amazon SageMaker Model Cards, Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluations, open source models, data, licensing

objectives.text: Identify tradeoffs between model safety and transparency
objectives.examples: measure interpretability and performance

objectives.text: Describe principles of human-centered design for explainable AI
objectives.examples: user-feedback mechanisms, AI decision transparency

objectives.text: Identify AWS services and features to secure AI systems
objectives.examples: IAM roles, policies, and permissions; encryption; Amazon Macie; AWS PrivateLink; AWS shared responsibility model; Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity; Policy in AgentCore; Amazon Bedrock Guardrails

objectives.text: Describe the concept of source citation and documenting data origins
objectives.examples: data lineage, data cataloging, Amazon SageMaker Model Cards

objectives.text: Describe best practices for secure data engineering
objectives.examples: assessing data quality, implementing privacy-enhancing technologies, data access control, data integrity

objectives.text: Describe security and privacy considerations for AI systems
objectives.examples: application security, threat detection, vulnerability management, infrastructure protection, prompt injection, encryption at rest and in transit, data leakage prevention, output filtering and validation, audit trail and logging requirements, toxicity

objectives.text: Describe hallucination detection methods and grounding techniques to improve output accuracy
objectives.examples: RAG grounding, output validation, confidence scoring

objectives.text: Identify AWS services and features to assist with governance and regulation compliance
objectives.examples: AWS Config, Amazon Inspector, AWS Artifact, AWS CloudTrail, AWS Trusted Advisor

objectives.text: Describe data governance strategies
objectives.examples: data lifecycles, logging, residency, monitoring, observation, retention

objectives.text: Describe processes to follow governance protocols
objectives.examples: policies, review cadence, review strategies, governance frameworks such as the Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix, transparency standards, team training requirements

notTested.why: The exam only tests today's narrow AI. Learn the difference so the word AI in a question never means sci-fi, but don't study it for the exam.
